query: My net trade income in a work year was negative. Can I trade the losses to offset my income in the following year to qualify for the Workfare Income Supplement (WIS) scheme?
reference_answer: Workfare Income Supplement (WIS) is based on your net trade income earned in the work year and does not include previous year's losses.

Given that the Workfare Income Supplement (WIS) is intended to supplement the income of lower-wage workers, it is most useful to assess the total income in determining one’s eligibility for WIS.

answer: No, you cannot trade losses from previous years to offset current year's income for Workfare Income Supplement (WIS) eligibility. According to [Document 1], WIS is based solely on the net trade income earned in the work year and does not consider previous year's losses.
